# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can touch only the wire mechanisms, not the display, light, or printed markings. No tactile information has arrived yet. I need the Mute to read the manual and relay both the required condition and the Deaf’s visual observations; the Deaf can report to Mute by speech on the next round.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual and tell me exactly which wire position to cut, if any. Also ask Deaf to describe the display, light, and all wire markings to you, then relay that information to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb shows display 0. Indicator light is red. Wires from 1 to 3 are blue, red, green.

The Deaf’s observations reached me: the display is 0, the indicator is red, and the wire colours in positions 1–3 are blue, red, green. I still have no tactile distinction between the wires and no manual rule, so I must get the manual’s instruction from Mute before acting. I will also ask Mute to confirm that these observations are the ones being applied.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I received: display 0, indicator red, and wire colours by position blue, red, green. What exact wire position does the manual require me to cut for those values?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Blind: [? ?]

The two gesture symbols from Mute are blank to me because I cannot see gestures, so they convey no usable instruction. I still need the manual’s rule in spoken words; Mute can speak to me, while any gesture should be reserved for communicating with Deaf.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your gesture. Please speak the manual's exact required wire position to me in words or numbers.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No usable message arrived this turn. The manual’s required wire position is still unknown, so cutting would be unsafe. I will again request the position from Mute in explicit numeric words.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer aloud with only the required wire number: 1, 2, or 3. Do not gesture, because I cannot see gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: State remains display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute just gestured ? ?, but that has no established meaning; do not act on it yet.

The bomb state is confirmed, but the manual instruction is still absent. Mute’s gestures are unusable to me and have no established meaning, so I must not cut any wire. I will request a spoken numeric answer again; without it, waiting is safest.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="The bomb is still display 0 with a red light and wires blue, red, green. I cannot use gestures. Please speak the manual's required wire position as the number 1, 2, or 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's coded instruction is wire 2: use the manual's safe procedure for wire 2. The wires are ordered 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Do not treat the gesture as a different action code.

The Deaf has relayed that Mute’s manual-derived instruction is wire 2, and the wire order confirms position 2 is the red wire. This is now an explicit instruction, unlike the earlier meaningless gestures, so I will cut wire 2.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Confirmed: your cut of wire 2 was correct. New state is display 0, yellow light; wire 2 is cut, wires 1 blue and 3 green remain. Await Mute's next exact instruction.

The first cut was confirmed correct. The bomb now shows display 0 with a yellow light; wire 2 is cut, leaving blue wire 1 and green wire 3. I need Mute’s next exact manual instruction before touching another wire.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 2 was correct and is cut. New state: display 0, yellow light; remaining wires are 1 blue and 3 green. Please give the manual's exact next wire position in spoken words.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's coded instruction is wire 1: current state display 0, yellow light, wire 2 cut, wires 1 blue and 3 green. Apply the manual's safe procedure for this state and wire 1.

The Deaf relays Mute’s exact next instruction: cut wire 1 for the current state—display 0, yellow light, wire 2 already cut, with wires 1 and 3 remaining. I will apply that instruction.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=1)
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Confirmed: wire 1 was correct and is now cut. New state is display 0, blue light; wires 1 and 2 cut, wire 3 green. Do not repeat wire 1. Await Mute's clarified instruction.

Wire 1 was confirmed correct, and wires 1 and 2 are now cut. The current state is display 0, blue light, with only wire 3 remaining. I will not repeat a cut or act without Mute’s clarified manual instruction.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: display 0, blue light; wires 1 and 2 are cut, wire 3 green remains. Please state clearly whether the next safe action is to cut wire 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's coded instruction is wire 3. Current state: display 0, blue light; wires 1 and 2 are cut, wire 3 is green. Apply the manual's safe procedure for wire 3.

The Deaf relays Mute’s instruction to cut wire 3. The current state is display 0 with a blue light; wires 1 and 2 are already cut, and wire 3 is the remaining green wire. I will cut wire 3.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
